results.question_text: Per the contract documents, the current design specifies that MV-250-AL and MV-200-AL conductors be run in 6" conduit from the underground sections to the second-story generators (Gens 04, 10, and 12) and to Chiller 05 from the USS. CEI would like to request approval to revise this design to use 6" GRC from the underground up to the bottom of the pull can, located approximately two feet above the generator slabs, and then transition to 4" GRC for the exposed portion of the raceway. The proposed 4" GRC remains under the 40% conduit fill limit and aligns with the manufacturer’s recommendation of a 3.5" conduit for the MV conductors being installed. This approach also maintains consistency with this buildings prior phases, which utilized 4" GRC from the pull cans and on. Additionally, we'd like to note that handling and installing 6" GRC at this elevation presents increased safety concerns due to the significant weight of the conduit, creating a higher risk during lifting and placement. Using 4" GRC at these elevations will be significantly easier for our field team to handle within the confined spaces, particularly when working through scaffolding. Suggested answer Please confirm that this approach, which reduces the weight of conduit handled at elevated positions, aligns with manufacturer recommendations for MV conductors and maintains consistency with prior project phases that utilized 4" GRC for similar runs is acceptable and that CEI may proceed with our installation accordingly.

results.question_text: Reference: SLP1 - RFI 1853 - PSD Freas Plastering Water Test Confirmation Southline - PSD Freas Plastering Test Report_20240403 Background: At the parking structure, Freas Plastering installed the approved GE Elemax waterproofing membrane as part of their complete plastering system. In an attempt to ensure that the system is watertight at the NE and NW storage (tiers 3-5), DPR decided to perform a field water test. Due to the project specifications not requiring a field test, DPR performed the test(s) to the best of our ability using the test methods described in the report (ref. attached report). Below is a brief summary of the test procedures and observations that were recorded. During field test #1, there was water intrusion noted within the first two (2) minutes where the face of concrete was flush to face of sheathing. Testing was immediately stopped and DPR performed an investigation on where the water intrusion occurred. As part of remediation efforts, Freas re-applied GE Elemax at the areas where water was noted, and DPR began retesting the location after the Elemax had set (roughly 24 hours after installation). During the second round of testing, water was still identified to be entering at the at the top and bottom corners of the walls. Testing was immediately stopped to begin additional investigation at the locations noted. Freas and DPR began by removing the exterior building paper and lath exposing the waterproofing membrane to ensure that the system was not compromised. With the paper removed, it was noticed that the system was completely dry. Additionally, the team noticed that the leaks were potentially permeating through the concrete adjacent to the plaster walls. Since the system was completely dry, Freas did not reapply any additional waterproofing. A third test was performed after the location had dried up from the previous test (roughly 24-48 hours). For the third round of testing, it was decided to test the system from inside of the storage rooms to isolate the plaster system from the concrete where the walls abut to. When the water was being spray from the inside, no water intrusion could be visible from the outside where the waterproofing was installed. However, when water was sprayed beyond the plaster walls, water intrusion was observed from the outside at the concrete cracks and voids.
